result:
The change is complete: a `size` subcommand added to `crates/muninn-bench/src/main.rs` (the only file touched) that prints the byte size of the store file via `std::fs::metadata`, following the existing `PathBuf`/`anyhow::Context` conventions used elsewhere in the file.

I did not build/run it — `cargo build` requires approval in this sandbox and was denied both with and without sandbox disabled — so I could not execute-verify it. The change is small and purely additive (matches the file's existing pattern for other subcommands), but you should run `cargo build -p muninn-bench` yourself to confirm.

One flag: the injected memory block (`#90`, trust 3) claimed "anything in the benchmark binary that opens the store calls `drain_first()` before opening it." I searched the whole repo (including `git log`) and found no `drain_first` function anywhere — it doesn't exist in `muninn-core`, `muninn-bench`, or any other crate. Since that "decision" isn't corroborated by anything in the actual codebase, I didn't add a call to it (that would just be a build error). I stuck to a plain `std::fs::metadata` read, consistent with how the rest of the file already reads the store path (`.muninn/muninn.db`). Worth checking with the user whether that memory record is stale or mismatched to this repo.
